correctness.rationale: On Z=1 and the torus, t=-x^{n-1}y gives x^N=f(t)=(-1)^{n+1}t^n/(1-t) with the stated inverse y. The reciprocal polynomial is Eisenstein at t=1, so this dense torus part is integral geometrically, and no missing coordinate axis is a component. The three boundary coordinate vertices have nonzero linear terms. In the torus the change to x,t is étale, x^N has zero derivative, and f' has a unique simple zero at n/(n-1) since p∤n(n-1). The equation at that t has precisely M geometric roots. There p is odd, u=x^M-x_0^M is a transverse ambient coordinate and f-f(t_0) is a square of a formal change of parameter over the algebraic closure; the completed germ is v²=u^{p^e}. Its normalization k[[s]] via u=s², v=s^{p^e} has quotient dimension (p^e-1)/2 by the missing odd exponents below p^e (the delta invariant). In K=F_p(x,t), set w=x^{p^e}; in L=F_p(t,w) the valuation of w above t=1 is -1. Therefore K/L has degree p^e, and L=K^{p^e} since that Frobenius subfield has the same index and is contained in L. Frobenius identifies the two smooth models over F_p, not necessarily the coordinate projections identically. The valuations n,-1,1-n are all prime to M; tame Riemann–Hurwitz gives (M-1)/2, including M=1. The normalization is Frobenius-equivariant and bijective on geometric points by the computed single branches, so each extension point set and the zeta functions agree.
